newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian shares seen flat or firmer on strong dlr.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian shares seen flat or firmer on strong dlr.

text.p: The strong dollar will be a driving factor on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Monday, traders said, predicting that this would result in a flat to firmer market after two days of downward correction.

"The dollar is very strong, Wall Street also firmed a little (on Friday), so I can expect the downward correction to weaken," said Marton Olah of Creditanstalt Securities. "I expect a quiet Monday with a flat market."
But another trader was more upbeat and said the dollar's rally might turn around the downward trend.
"The dollar's rise will have a strongly positive impact on the market," said Tamas Revesz of Wintrust.

The Hungarian forint opened at 190.75/80 to the dollar, well down from Friday's close of 189.04/09, as a result of the U.S. currency's gains since Friday. A strong dollar makes the forint, and thus Hungarian shares, cheaper for foreign buyers.
The corporate side seems to be quiet, with market participants looking forward to the release of first half corporate earnings which have to be submitted to the stock exchange by August 15.
On Monday, the Central Statistical Office (KSH) is expected to release the final industrial output figures for May.
On Friday the BUX index finished at 7,162.40 points, down 56.80.
